questions.conventional:
> ![](/tmp/import-bzoi1s3c/media/image3.png){width="1.9680555555555554in" height="1.0743055555555556in"}Here D and d are constant.

> The stone comes to a momentary rest and reverses its direction of motion at time $v_{0}/g$.

Gravity g points down.](data/figures/P000116-stem-1.62d89317.png)A vertical projectile experiences a retarding acceleration of $a$ opposite to the direction of motion of the projectile. (i) Time of ascent

(iii) Maximum height reached
(iv) Speed just before it hits the ground

questions.answer: $t_{a} = \frac{u}{g + a}$; $t_{d} = \frac{u}{g - a}$; Max height H: $\frac{u^{2}}{2(g + a)}$; Speed at C: $\sqrt{2(g - a)H} = u\sqrt{\frac{g - a}{g + a}}$; (v) Point D: the speed at D (going up) is greater than at E (coming down), because the retarding acceleration removes speed throughout the flight
hints: > Net downward acceleration during upward motion (A – B): $(g + a)$, and $(g - a)$ during downward motion.

questions.conventional:
> Displacement of cyclist has to be 96 m compared to displacement of bus at time t

> First cyclist will overtake the bus at t = 8 sec when the speed of bus is 16 m/s (less than cyclist)

questions.conventional:
> The speed gained by ball A will be equal to speed lost by B at any instant

>

> If speed of B at the instant of collision is u, then speed of A will be 2u

>

> Speed of projection of B = u + Speed lost (2u) = 3u

>

> Average speed of A: u and average speed of B is 2u hence B will travel 2/3 of the distance

questions.question: A particle starts from rest and moves along the x-axis with acceleration ‘a’ at time ‘t’ given by $a = a_{0}(1 - \frac{t}{T})$. Find average velocity during the time interval $t = 0$ to $t = T$?

> Average velocity during a time interval = (Displacement / time)

>

> $\frac{dv}{dt} = a_{0}(1 - \frac{t}{T})$; on integration $v = a_{0}(t - \frac{t^{2}}{2T})$

>

> Further integration $\mathrm{\Delta}x = a_{0}\frac{T^{2}}{3}$

The acceleration–displacement graph of the bicycle's motion is best described by:
![Four graphs of acceleration a in m/s² against x in m, labelled A to D, with 2 and 10 marked on the a-axis and 200 and 400 on the x-axis. A rises in a curve to 10 at 200, then stays at 10. B rises in a straight line from 2 to 10 at 200, then drops to zero. C rises in a straight line from 2 to 10 at 200, then stays at 10. D rises in a curve from 2 to 10 at 200 and stops there.](data/figures/P000169-stem-2.d68019b2.png)
hints:
> Key Concept: 0 – 200 m, straight line $\rightarrow$ $\frac{dv}{dx}$ is constant; hence use $a = v\frac{dv}{dx} = v \times constant$

>

> Here v = 10 + 0.2x, so a = 0.2v = 2 + 0.04x: a straight line rising from 2 m/s² at x = 0 to 10 m/s² at x = 200 m; beyond 200 m, v is constant and a = 0.

questions.conventional:
> Let us focus on downward motion (fall from h) with $x$ being the distance fallen

>

> Option B: the speed increases at increasing rate as it falls (slope of tangent gets steeper as ‘h’ decreases)

>

> Option C: speed increases linearly

>

> Option D: it increases at decreasing rate

>

> The key is to find the relationship between $v - x$ which is $v = \sqrt{2gx}$

>

> $\frac{dv}{dx}\  \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{x}}$ or the velocity will keep increasing at decreasing rate (increase in speed for a unit fall will keep decreasing as it falls)
